mechanism_claims.claim_text: Bac7/Bac7PS are proline-rich antimicrobial peptides with intracellular ribosomal/protein-translation inhibition context; Bac7PS remains a strong bacterial ribosomal inhibitor.
direct_assay_types: in vitro translation inhibition assay with E. coli S30 extract
mechanism_claims.limitations: Bac7PS showed a nonsignificant mean shift for E. coli ribosome inhibition and a larger HEK293 ribosome shift only at much higher concentrations; no unsupported exact curve values were digitized.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Bac7PS activity is less dependent on the SbmA transporter than Bac71-23 based on the BW25113 ΔsbmA MIC comparison.
direct_assay_types: MIC comparison in E. coli BW25113 and BW25113 ΔsbmA
mechanism_claims.limitations: This supports reduced transporter dependency, not a full uptake-pathway mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The improved Bac7PS activity is not explained by membrane lysis at MIC; membrane damage is low at MIC with only minor high-concentration membrane damage noted.
direct_assay_types: GFP loss/propidium iodide membrane damage assay
mechanism_claims.limitations: Figure-only membrane damage curves were used qualitatively; exact curve series were not fabricated from images.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Bac7PS showed in vivo efficacy in a murine septicemia model induced by E. coli ATCC 25922.
mechanism_claims.limitations: This is efficacy evidence, not a direct molecular mechanism claim.
